title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
description: Problem: While ForceVLA demonstrates the value of 6-axis wrist force-torque sensing, it captures only aggregate contact wrench information and cannot localize contact distribution across finger surfaces—critical for in-hand manipulation tasks like re-grasping, rotating objects, or precision assembly where fingertip contact geometry matters. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-resolution distributed tactile sensor arrays (e.g., GelSight or BioTac-style sensors providing ~100 taxel readings per fingertip) into a VLA framework. Rather than a MoE fusion module, we propose a Tactile Tokenizer that compresses spatial pressure maps into compact latent tokens via a convolutional VAE pretrained on a large tactile-manipulation corpus, then cross-attends these tokens with vision-language embeddings inside the action decoder. A contact-aware curriculum progressively introduces tactile noise and partial sensor occlusion during training to improve robustness. We also construct TactileManip-Data: 10,000 demonstrations across 8 tasks (bolt tightening, card sliding, marble rolling, fragile object grasping) with synchronized RGB, depth, proprioception, and per-fingertip tactile streams. Experiments: Compare against ForceVLA, pi_0, and ablations removing tactile tokenization or curriculum on both in-distribution and zero-shot object transfer tasks, measuring success rate, contact stability metrics, and object slip frequency.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizable Contact-Rich Manipulation via Distributed Tactile Sensing and Uncertainty-Aware Action Decoding
description:
Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors, which provide global contact wrench measurements but lack spatial resolution about where and how contact occurs across the manipulator surface. For tasks requiring fingertip dexterity (e.g., in-hand reorientation, compliant grasping of deformable objects), spatially distributed tactile feedback is essential but remains absent from current VLA frameworks.

Method: We propose TactileVLA, which augments a VLA backbone (π0) with high-resolution fingertip tactile arrays (e.g., GelSight or DIGIT sensors) as a new sensory modality. We design a Tactile Patch Transformer that tokenizes spatial pressure maps into compact embeddings, fused with visual-language tokens via cross-attention. Critically, we introduce an uncertainty-aware action head that models epistemic uncertainty over contact state estimates, gating motor commands when tactile evidence is ambiguous—enabling safe recovery behaviors.

Experiments: We evaluate on five dexterous tasks: fragile object grasping, in-hand pen reorientation, cable threading, compliant assembly, and Braille reading. We compare against ForceVLA, vanilla VLA, and tactile-only baselines. Ablations examine tactile tokenization resolution, uncertainty gating thresholds, and sim-to-real transfer using tactile simulation. Success rates, contact safety violations, and recovery rates are primary metrics.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description:
Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates that wrist-mounted 6-axis force/torque sensing significantly improves contact-rich manipulation, but a single F/T sensor provides only aggregated contact information, failing to localize contact distribution across tool surfaces or robot links—critical for tasks like sliding objects along walls, cloth folding, or bimanual assembly where contact geometry matters.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, extending VLA models with spatially-distributed tactile sensing via high-density resistive tactile arrays mounted on robot fingertips and palm surfaces (~100 taxels per finger). Rather than MoE fusion of a single force vector, we propose a Tactile Tokenizer that converts spatially-indexed pressure maps into learned patch tokens (analogous to ViT image patches), which are appended to the VLA's transformer context alongside vision-language tokens. We train a spatial contact attention module that learns which contact regions are task-relevant for action decoding.

Planned Experiments: (1) Collect a TactileVLA-Data dataset across 6 tasks: peg-in-hole, bolt tightening, dough kneading, garment folding, cable routing, and fragile object grasping. (2) Ablate tactile tokenization resolution and placement (fingertip-only vs. full palm). (3) Compare against ForceVLA-style single F/T baselines and vision-only π0. (4) Evaluate zero-shot transfer to novel object geometries where visual appearance provides insufficient contact feedback.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description:
Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force sensing at the wrist, but many manipulation tasks (cloth folding, deformable object handling, bimanual assembly) require spatially distributed contact information across the robot's entire end-effector or finger surfaces—information that 6-axis wrist F/T sensors cannot provide. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which incorporates readings from a 16x16 taxel tactile sensor array (e.g., GelSight or BioTac-SP) on the robot's palm and fingertips. These are fused into a pretrained VLA (π0-based) via cross-attention with language and visual tokens, without MoE routing, instead using learned soft-gating based on task phase detection.

Experiments: (1) Five dexterous tasks: garment folding, in-hand rotation, plug insertion, peg-in-hole, fragile object grasping. (2) Ablations comparing: no tactile, wrist F/T only (ForceVLA-style), tactile-only, combined tactile+F/T. (3) Generalization to unseen object materials and geometries. (4) Occlusion robustness benchmarks where vision is fully blocked. We collect a TactileVLA-Dataset with synchronized RGB, tactile maps, and proprioception across 3000 demonstrations.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizable Contact-Rich Manipulation via Skin-Inspired Distributed Tactile Sensing in Vision-Language-Action Models

title: TactileVLA: Unified Spatial Tactile-Vision-Language-Action Models for In-Hand Manipulation via Fingertip Sensor Arrays

title: TactileVLA: Transferring Contact Intelligence Across Robot Morphologies via Cross-Embodiment Force-Tactile Foundation Models
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates that force sensing dramatically improves contact-rich manipulation, but force-torque data is expensive to collect and models trained on one robot morphology (e.g., 6-DOF arm with wrist F/T sensor) fail to transfer to different embodiments (e.g., dexterous hands with distributed tactile sensors or mobile manipulators). This severely limits scalability of force-aware VLA systems. Proposed Method: We develop TactileVLA, a cross-embodiment force-tactile foundation model that learns a universal contact representation space bridging heterogeneous sensing modalities—wrist F/T sensors, fingertip tactile arrays, and joint torque estimates. The core innovation is a sensor-agnostic contact tokenizer using masked autoencoding across modalities, trained contrastively to align representations from different sensor types during the same physical interaction. A lightweight embodiment adapter then conditions a shared VLA backbone on morphology-specific contact tokens without full fine-tuning. Experiments: (1) Zero-shot transfer of ForceVLA-Data trained policies to a Shadow Hand with BioTac sensors on analogous tasks; (2) Cross-embodiment few-shot adaptation (10 demos) vs. full retraining baselines; (3) Sim-to-real transfer using simulated tactile signals as bridge modality; (4) Ablations on contrastive alignment strategies and adapter architectures. Success metric: >60% task success with <20 real-world demonstrations on target embodiment.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial Attention Routing

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Reasoning
description:

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description:
Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force/torque sensing into VLA models, but many manipulation tasks—cloth folding, compliant assembly, human-robot handovers—require distributed tactile feedback across the entire hand or arm surface, not just endpoint wrench signals. Single-point force sensing misses spatial contact geometry critical for dexterous in-hand manipulation.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which replaces the single F/T sensor with a distributed tactile skin array (e.g., 64-taxel fingertip + palm sensors) and designs a Spatial Tactile Encoder (STE) using sparse graph neural networks to aggregate taxel readings into contact-map embeddings. These embeddings are fused with VLA visual-language tokens via a lightweight cross-attention adapter, bypassing the need for MoE routing by instead learning contact-geometry-conditioned action residuals on top of a frozen pi_0 backbone.

Experiments: (1) In-hand object reorientation (five object categories, sim-to-real transfer), (2) Cloth manipulation requiring distributed pressure sensing, (3) Deformable object insertion where wrist F/T alone is insufficient. We compare against ForceVLA (wrist F/T), proprioception-only VLA, and raw tactile concatenation baselines, measuring success rate, contact stability metrics, and generalization to unseen object geometries. Dataset of 2,000 demonstrations with synchronized tactile maps is collected and released.

title: TactileVLA: Skin-Distributed Tactile Sensing as a Scalable Modality for Generalizable Contact Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates that wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors improve contact-rich manipulation, but single-point force measurements fail to capture spatially distributed contact events (e.g., multi-finger grasping, cloth folding, surface sliding). Distributed tactile skin provides rich spatial pressure maps but remains unexplored as a VLA modality. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-resolution tactile skin arrays (e.g., 16x16 taxel patches per finger) into a VLA framework via a novel Spatial Tactile Tokenizer (STT). STT compresses 2D pressure maps into compact learned tokens using a convolutional encoder pretrained via masked autoencoding on a new tactile pretraining corpus. These tokens are fused into the VLA's action-decoding transformer via cross-attention alongside vision-language embeddings, without requiring a MoE router—instead relying on attention to dynamically weight modalities. We introduce TactileVLA-Bench: 6 tasks requiring spatial contact discrimination (peg-in-hole with tolerances <1mm, fragile object grasping, fabric manipulation, door latch, cable routing, bolt tightening). Experiments compare: (1) baseline VLA, (2) ForceVLA-style F/T fusion, (3) TactileVLA, and (4) TactileVLA+F/T combined, measuring success rate, contact force compliance, and generalization to novel object geometries. We hypothesize spatial tactile maps provide complementary information to scalar F/T signals, yielding +15% additional improvement on spatially sensitive tasks.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizable Contact-Rich Manipulation via Skin-Distributed Tactile Sensing in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:
Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, which provides global contact wrench information but lacks spatial resolution about where and how contact distributes across the robot's hand or tool surface. Tasks like in-hand re-grasping, sliding objects along surfaces, or manipulating deformable items require spatially-resolved tactile feedback unavailable from a single F/T sensor.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, extending VLA models with distributed high-resolution tactile skin signals. We design a Tactile Tokenizer that encodes spatiotemporal patterns from a fingertip/palm taxel array (e.g., GelSight or capacitive skin with ~100 sensing elements) into compact latent tokens via a convolutional temporal encoder. These tactile tokens are fused into the VLA action decoder using a lightweight cross-attention layer, conditioned on language instructions to select task-relevant contact regions dynamically. Unlike MoE routing over modalities, our approach performs instruction-conditioned spatial attention over tactile patches, enabling grounded physical reasoning (e.g., 'which finger feels slipping').

Experiments: (1) Collect TactileVLA-Data: 5 tasks including in-hand rotation, slip recovery, peg-in-hole, cloth folding, and jar opening with synchronized RGB, proprioception, and tactile arrays. (2) Compare against ForceVLA, pi_0 baseline, and ablations removing tactile or attention conditioning. (3) Evaluate zero-shot transfer to novel object geometries to assess generalization from spatial contact patterns.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizable Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sparse Tactile Skin Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:
Problem: ForceVLA improves VLA models with wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors, but these provide only aggregate contact information at the end-effector. Many dexterous tasks (in-hand reorientation, compliant grasping of deformable objects, multi-finger manipulation) require spatially-distributed contact sensing across the finger surfaces—information that wrist F/T sensors cannot provide. Existing tactile-skin-equipped robots lack principled integration with large VLA foundations.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates sparse tactile skin arrays (e.g., 4×4 pressure patches on each fingertip) into a VLA backbone via a novel Tactile Tokenizer that encodes spatial contact pressure maps into compact tokens using a lightweight convolutional encoder. These tactile tokens are fused with visual-language embeddings through cross-attention before action decoding, without requiring MoE routing overhead. We additionally propose a Tactile Dropout curriculum during training to handle sensor occlusion and partial contact, improving generalization to unseen object geometries.

Experiments: (1) In-hand reorientation of rigid and deformable objects; (2) Fragile object grasping with force constraints; (3) Cloth folding requiring distributed contact awareness. We compare against ForceVLA (wrist F/T only), vision-only VLA baselines, and ablations removing tactile tokenization. We evaluate success rate, force limit violations, and zero-shot transfer to novel objects across 6 tasks on a dexterous robot hand platform.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial-Temporal Graph Experts
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force-torque sensing for contact-rich manipulation, but wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors provide only aggregate contact information, missing the spatially distributed contact geometry critical for dexterous tasks like in-hand reorientation, grasp adjustment, or multi-finger assembly. title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial Graph Attention for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
description:

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Self-Supervised Pre-Training of Distributed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich VLA Policies
description:

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for In-Hand Manipulation
description:
Problem: While ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, it lacks spatially distributed contact information critical for in-hand manipulation tasks like regrasping, pivoting, or tool-use, where contact location and pressure distribution across finger surfaces matter as much as aggregate wrench measurements.

Critically, we introduce contact-aware curriculum learning: training progressively from gross grasping to fine in-hand repositioning, using tactile signals to define automatic task difficulty metrics.

Experiments: We evaluate on five in-hand manipulation benchmarks (object reorientation, card insertion, bolt tightening, fragile object handling, tool handover), comparing against ForceVLA, pi_0+FT, and vision-only baselines. title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Pretraining of Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Representation Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Skin Representations in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Pretraining of Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing for In-Hand Manipulation

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Multi-Finger Tactile Sensing Integration for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation via Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
description: Problem: While ForceVLA demonstrates that wrist-mounted force-torque sensing improves contact-rich manipulation, whole-hand dexterous tasks (reorienting objects, tool use, handovers) require distributed tactile feedback across multiple fingertips. Naively extending force-aware fusion to high-dimensional multi-finger tactile arrays (e.g., 5 fingers × 16 taxels = 80 channels) creates modality explosion and routing instability in MoE frameworks. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which processes per-finger tactile signals through lightweight convolutional encoders producing compact 'tactile tokens,' then routes these tokens through a Sparse Topological MoE (ST-MoE) where expert selection is conditioned on both language task embeddings and contact topology (which fingers are active). A contact-topology gate suppresses inactive finger experts, keeping compute tractable. The fused tactile-visual-language representation conditions a flow-matching action decoder. We additionally collect TactileVLA-Data: 8 dexterous manipulation tasks using a multi-finger hand equipped with BioTac-like sensors, with synchronized vision, tactile, and proprioceptive streams. Experiments: (1) ablation of per-finger vs. aggregate tactile encoding; (2) topology-gating vs. standard top-k routing; (3) cross-task generalization to unseen object geometries; (4) sim-to-real transfer using tactile domain randomization. Baselines include ForceVLA adapted to fingertip sensing, ACT+tactile, and DexVLA.

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Self-Supervised Pre-training of Tactile Representations for Vision-Language-Action Models via Cross-Modal Masked Reconstruction
description:
Problem: ForceVLA relies on wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors that provide global contact wrench but lack spatial resolution about where and how contact distributes across a gripper surface. This forces the tactile encoder to learn contact semantics grounded in object appearance and task intent. At fine-tuning time, the frozen tactile encoder is plugged into a π₀-based VLA backbone via a lightweight cross-attention adapter—no MoE routing needed, reducing deployment complexity.

Planned Experiments: (1) Collect 50-hour dataset across 8 dexterous tasks (peg insertion, fabric folding, fragile object grasping) with DIGIT sensors on a bimanual setup. (2) Compare success rates against ForceVLA, pure F/T baselines, and vision-only VLA. (3) Ablate masking ratio, cross-modal conditioning, and frozen vs. fine-tuned encoder. (4) Evaluate generalization to novel object textures and under visual occlusion.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Touch-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Control via Distributed Tactile Skin Integration for Deformable Object Manipulation
description:

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Pretraining of Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Reasoning
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force-torque sensing at the wrist for contact-rich manipulation, but single-point F/T signals cannot capture spatially distributed contact patterns required for tasks involving whole-hand grasping, surface following, or object deformation estimation. title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Skin-Distributed Tactile Sensing with Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque (F/T) signals, which provide global contact wrench information but lack spatial resolution about where and how contact distributes across the robot's fingers and palm. Experiments: Compare vs. ForceVLA and vision-only VLA baselines on (1) deformable object grasping, (2) in-hand rotation, (3) slip recovery, measuring success rate, contact efficiency, and expert activation sparsity.

title: TactileVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors, which provide aggregate contact information but lack spatial resolution across the hand surface. Experiments: (1) Ablations on tactile spatial resolution vs. task success; (2) Comparison against ForceVLA and proprioception-only baselines; (3) Zero-shot transfer to novel object geometries; (4) Occlusion-heavy scenarios where vision alone is insufficient. title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
description:
Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors, but contact-rich in-hand manipulation (e.g., regrasping, tool use, deformable object handling) requires spatially distributed tactile information across finger surfaces—information a single wrist F/T sensor cannot provide. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which encodes multi-fingertip tactile maps using a lightweight spatial CNN tokenizer, producing compact tactile patch tokens analogous to visual patch tokens. These tactile tokens are fused with vision-language embeddings via a cross-modal attention layer inserted at each action decoding step. To handle asynchronous, sparse tactile events, we propose an event-driven tactile tokenizer that only encodes fingertips experiencing significant contact pressure changes, reducing computational overhead. We pretrain the tactile encoder on a curated dataset of 50K contact episodes using self-supervised contrastive learning across tactile-visual pairs.

Experiments: We evaluate on four dexterous tasks—in-hand rotation, screwdriving, card insertion, and grape grasping—using a Shadow Dexterous Hand with BioTac sensors. Ablations compare full tactile arrays vs. F/T-only vs. no haptics. Baselines include ForceVLA and standard π0. Primary metrics: task success rate, object slip frequency, and generalization to unseen object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing for In-Hand Manipulation
description: Problem: While ForceVLA demonstrates the value of wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors for contact-rich manipulation, such sensors provide only aggregate contact information at a single point. Experiments: (1) Dexterous in-hand reorientation on 10 object geometries; (2) Slip detection and recovery during grasping of deformable/slippery objects; (3) Blind peg-in-hole under full visual occlusion; (4) Ablations comparing aggregate F/T-only vs. distributed tactile vs. combined sensing; (5) Zero-shot transfer to novel object textures. title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description:
Problem: While ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors into VLA models, whole-body manipulation tasks (e.g., cloth folding, deformable object handling, human-robot handovers) require spatially distributed contact information across the robot's surface. A single F/T sensor cannot localize contact geometry or distinguish multi-point contact patterns essential for these tasks.

Method: We propose TactileVLA, which integrates high-density resistive tactile skin arrays (covering fingers, palm, and forearm) as a new spatial contact modality into a VLA backbone. Rather than MoE routing on scalar force signals, we introduce a Tactile Patch Tokenizer that converts 2D tactile pressure maps into spatial tokens using a ViT-style encoder pretrained via masked tactile modeling. These tactile tokens are fused with visual and language tokens through cross-modal attention layers inserted into the action decoder, enabling spatially-aware contact reasoning.

Experiments: (1) Cloth manipulation benchmark: folding, hanging, bagging. (2) Deformable object insertion: soft connectors, irregular-shaped plugs. (3) Human-robot object handover under occlusion. We compare against ForceVLA (F/T only), vision-only baselines, and ablations removing spatial vs. temporal tactile information. Primary metrics: task success rate, contact localization accuracy, and graceful failure rate under unexpected contact perturbations.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Skin-Inspired Distributed Tactile Sensing in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: ForceVLA uses centralized 6-axis wrist force-torque sensing, which provides aggregate contact information but cannot localize where on the manipulator contact occurs or characterize contact geometry. Distributed fingertip/palm tactile arrays (e.g., GelSight, capacitive skin) provide spatially-resolved contact maps critical for tasks like in-hand reorientation, sliding grasp adjustment, or multi-finger coordination — yet no VLA framework integrates them systematically. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which encodes distributed tactile sensor arrays (16x16 pressure maps per finger) as spatial 'tactile tokens' via a lightweight CNN encoder, then injects these into a VLA backbone (based on pi_0) alongside vision-language tokens via a cross-attention tactile fusion layer. Unlike ForceVLA's MoE routing on scalar force signals, we propose a spatial attention gating mechanism that learns which spatial contact regions are task-relevant at each decoding step. We also introduce curriculum-based sim-to-real tactile domain randomization to bridge the sim-to-real gap. Experiments: We evaluate on five in-hand manipulation tasks (peg rotation, card sliding, bolt tightening, deformable object squeezing, multi-finger handover) in simulation (IsaacGym with tactile plugins) and on a real Allegro hand. Ablations compare centralized force sensing, tactile tokens, and spatial gating. Primary metric: task success rate and contact slip events.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA improves contact-rich manipulation using a single wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensor, but many dexterous tasks (cloth folding, deformable object handling, multi-contact assembly) require spatially distributed contact information across the robot's fingers, palm, and arm. A single F/T sensor cannot localize contact points or capture rich tactile texture/slip signals needed for such tasks. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-density resistive tactile skin arrays (e.g., 64-taxel finger arrays + 128-taxel palm patches) as a new sensory modality into a VLA backbone. Rather than a single F/T vector, we encode spatial tactile maps via a lightweight convolutional tactile encoder producing patch-level embeddings. We propose a Hierarchical Tactile-Visual-Language Fusion (HTVLF) module that first spatially aligns tactile patches with visual fingertip regions via cross-attention, then routes fused contact representations through task-conditioned experts for action decoding. A contact-anticipation auxiliary loss predicts expected tactile patterns before contact, improving proactive rather than reactive control. Experiments: We collect a 5-task dataset including garment folding, cable routing, deformable insertion, and fragile object grasping with synchronized RGB, tactile maps, and proprioception. We compare against ForceVLA, vanilla VLA, and ablations removing spatial encoding or cross-modal alignment, measuring task success rate, contact localization accuracy, and slip/break incidents.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Signals with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial Graph Experts
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates a single 6-axis wrist force-torque sensor, but many dexterous tasks (in-hand manipulation, multi-finger grasping, surface following) require spatially distributed tactile information across the entire hand surface. A single global force reading cannot localize contact geometry or distinguish which fingertip is slipping. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which equips a robot hand with a distributed tactile skin array (e.g., 48-taxel fingertip sensors per finger) and proposes a Spatial Tactile Graph Expert (STGE) module. Each fingertip's taxel array is encoded via a small spatial CNN into a tactile patch embedding; these embeddings form nodes in a contact graph where edges represent adjacency and kinematic coupling. A Graph Attention Network aggregates spatial contact context and feeds per-region expert tokens into a MoE adapter within a frozen VLA backbone (pi_0), routing based on both linguistic intent and contact topology. We also construct TactileVLA-Data: 8 in-hand tasks (bolt-tightening, card insertion, fragile object handling, peg-in-hole with rotation) with synchronized RGB, proprioception, and 240-taxel signals. Experiments compare against ForceVLA-style wrist-only baselines, ablate graph topology vs. pooled tactile features, and evaluate on slip-recovery under visual occlusion. Target metric: >25% improvement in manipulation success on deformable and rotationally-constrained insertion tasks.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Synthesis and Cross-Sensor Policy Transfer
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates that wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors significantly improve contact-rich manipulation, but such sensors are expensive, fragile, and not universally available across robot platforms. A more accessible alternative is dense tactile sensing (e.g., vision-based tactile sensors like GelSight), yet no framework exists to unify heterogeneous tactile modalities within VLA systems or enable cross-sensor policy transfer. Proposed Method: We propose TactileVLA, which (1) builds a physics-based tactile signal synthesis pipeline to generate diverse GelSight-style contact images from simulated contact geometry and F/T readings, enabling cheap simulation data augmentation; (2) introduces a modality-agnostic tactile encoder using contrastive alignment to map both F/T signals and tactile images into a shared 'contact embedding space'; and (3) integrates this shared embedding into a pi_0-based VLA via a lightweight cross-attention adapter, enabling zero-shot sensor-type transfer at deployment. Experiments: We evaluate on (a) the ForceVLA-Data benchmark using GelSight sensors instead of F/T sensors to test cross-sensor transfer, (b) novel tasks like fabric folding and surface texture-guided grasping where spatial contact distribution matters, and (c) ablations comparing modality-agnostic vs. sensor-specific encoders, measuring success rate, contact force compliance, and generalization to unseen object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Augmentation for Vision-Language-Action Models
description:
Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force-torque sensing for contact-rich manipulation, but 6-axis F/T sensors are expensive, fragile, and difficult to deploy on dexterous multi-fingered hands where distributed tactile feedback is more informative. Most real-world manipulation platforms lack wrist F/T sensors entirely, limiting adoption of force-aware VLA approaches.

Proposed Method: We propose TactileVLA, which replaces wrist F/T sensing with high-resolution fingertip tactile arrays (e.g., DIGIT sensors) and introduces a Tactile-to-Force Distillation (TFD) module. During training in simulation, we pair rich tactile observations with ground-truth contact forces/torques to train a lightweight tactile encoder that produces force-equivalent embeddings. At deployment, only tactile sensors are needed. We integrate these embeddings into a VLA backbone (π0) using a cross-modal attention adapter rather than MoE routing, reducing inference overhead. A synthetic tactile augmentation pipeline generates diverse contact scenarios in IsaacGym to improve sim-to-real transfer.

Experiments: (1) Compare TactileVLA vs. ForceVLA-style F/T baseline on five contact-rich tasks (peg insertion, cable routing, jar opening, card swiping, connector mating). (2) Ablate tactile encoder architectures and distillation objectives. (3) Evaluate generalization to novel object geometries and compliant surfaces. (4) Measure performance under visual occlusion where tactile signals are uniquely informative.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque (F/T) sensors into VLA models, but wrist F/T provides only aggregate contact information. title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial Attention Routing
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing into VLA models, but a single force sensor provides only aggregate contact information and cannot localize where on the hand/fingers contact occurs. Distributed tactile sensor arrays (e.g., fingertip taxels) capture spatially-resolved contact maps critical for tasks like in-hand re-orientation, delicate grasping of deformable objects, and multi-finger assembly. These tokens are injected into the VLA's action decoder via a learned Spatial Tactile Attention Router (STAR) that attends differently to finger-specific contact regions depending on the current task phase inferred from language context. Unlike MoE routing in ForceVLA, STAR performs spatial-semantic cross-attention between language embeddings and per-finger tactile patches, enabling finger-level adaptive control. Experiments: We collect a new dataset with a 3-finger tactile-equipped hand spanning five tasks (in-hand rotation, deformable insertion, cloth folding, peg-in-hole, fruit picking). We compare against ForceVLA-style aggregate force integration, raw tactile concatenation, and pi0 baselines, evaluating success rate, contact localization accuracy, and generalization to novel object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial Graph Experts
description: Problem: While ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing into VLA models, this single-point measurement misses the rich spatial distribution of contact information available from multi-fingered tactile sensor arrays (e.g., GelSight, DIGIT sensors across fingertips). Tasks like in-hand object reorientation, slip detection, and deformable object manipulation require knowing where and how contact occurs across the entire grasp surface, not just aggregate wrench. A Graph Attention Network processes this tactile graph into spatially-aware contact embeddings, which are fused with VLA visual-language tokens via a new Spatial Contact MoE (SC-MoE). Unlike ForceVLA's single-modality force router, SC-MoE routes based on both contact location and intensity patterns, enabling experts to specialize in fingertip-specific or whole-hand contact regimes. We augment the action head with a slip-prediction auxiliary loss using tactile temporal gradients. Experiments: (1) In-hand reorientation of novel objects, (2) Peg insertion with finger-level contact feedback, (3) Deformable object squeezing to target stiffness. Baselines include ForceVLA, pi_0, and tactile-only controllers. We evaluate generalization to unseen object geometries and materials.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact-Rich Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force sensing at the wrist, but contact-rich manipulation often requires distributed tactile feedback across the entire robot hand and arm surface. Single 6-axis F/T sensors cannot localize contact or capture slip, shear, and pressure distributions across fingers and palm during dexterous grasping and in-hand manipulation. title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Dense Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact-Rich Manipulation
description:

Dense tactile skin arrays (e.g., GelSight, BioTac, or capacitive taxel arrays) provide spatially-resolved contact maps critical for tasks like in-hand object re-orientation, deformable object handling, and safe human-robot handovers—yet no VLA framework incorporates them.

These tokens are fused with visual-language embeddings via a cross-attention mechanism at the action decoding stage, conditioned on contact phase detection (pre-contact, grasp, manipulation). We collect TactileVLA-Data: 3,000 demonstrations across six tasks (in-hand rotation, cloth folding, peg-in-hole, fragile object grasping, handover, zip fastening) with synchronized RGB, tactile maps, proprioception, and wrist F/T.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Simulated-to-Real Tactile Skin Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:
Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force-torque sensing, but 6-axis F/T sensors only capture aggregate wrist-level contact information, missing spatially distributed contact patterns crucial for tasks like cloth folding, soft object handling, or multi-finger grasping where localized pressure distribution matters.

To overcome scarce real tactile data, we develop a sim-to-real tactile transfer pipeline using differentiable tactile simulation (TACTO) with domain randomization, pre-training the SCT on simulated contact scenarios before fine-tuning on 500 real demonstrations.

Experiments: (1) Compare TactileVLA vs. ForceVLA vs. baseline π0 on cloth folding, peg-in-hole with deformable pegs, fragile object grasping, and garment insertion; (2) Ablate SCT resolution vs. simple flattened vectors; (3) Evaluate sim-to-real transfer quality with varying amounts of real data (10/50/500 demos); (4) Test generalization to unseen object deformability levels.

title: TactileVLA: Grounding Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for In-Hand Manipulation
description:

Wrist F/T sensors cannot distinguish which fingertip is contacting or measure local slip — critical for dexterous regrasping.

Experiments: We collect TactileVLA-Data with a three-fingered hand equipped with BioTac/DIGIT sensors across six in-hand tasks. Ablations compare: no tactile, wrist F/T only (ForceVLA-style), and full tactile skin. title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
description:
Problem: While ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensing into VLA models, contact-rich in-hand manipulation (reorienting, pivoting, regrasping objects) requires spatially distributed tactile information across finger surfaces—something a single wrist sensor cannot provide. Existing VLA models lack mechanisms to process high-dimensional, spatially structured tactile arrays (e.g., 16x16 taxel grids per fingertip) alongside vision and language.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which encodes multi-fingertip tactile arrays using a lightweight spatial CNN tokenizer that produces per-finger tactile tokens, analogous to image patch tokens. These tactile tokens are injected into a pretrained VLA backbone (π0 or OpenVLA) via cross-attention layers at each action decoding step. Rather than MoE routing, we employ a contact-conditioned gating mechanism: tactile tokens are upweighted only when contact pressure exceeds a learned threshold, preventing noise injection during free-space motion. A contact-map prediction auxiliary head jointly trained with action prediction encourages spatially grounded tactile representations.

Experiments: (1) In-hand reorientation of 20 unseen objects; (2) Screwing/unscrewing bolts under visual occlusion; (3) Fragile object handling with force limits. We compare against wrist-F/T-only (ForceVLA-style), vision-only VLA, and tactile-as-flattened-vector baselines, measuring success rate, grasp stability, and object damage frequency on a dexterous hand platform.

title: TactileVLA: Integrating Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing into Vision-Language-Action Models for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
description:
Problem: While ForceVLA demonstrates the value of wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, contact-rich in-hand manipulation (reorientation, regrasping, tool use) requires spatially distributed tactile feedback across the entire finger surface—information that aggregate force signals fundamentally cannot provide. Existing VLA models lack mechanisms to process high-dimensional, spatially structured tactile arrays.

Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates fingertip tactile sensor arrays (e.g., GelSight or DIGIT sensors providing ~100 tactile patches per finger) into a VLA backbone. We design a Tactile Spatial Tokenizer (TST) that encodes per-finger pressure maps into compact patch tokens via a lightweight convolutional encoder, producing spatially-aware embeddings. These tokens are fused with vision-language embeddings through a cross-attention module before action decoding, enabling the model to reason about contact geometry and slip detection. We also explore using tactile signals as a reward signal for online adaptation during deployment.

Experiments: (1) Collect a dataset of 10 in-hand manipulation tasks (pen spinning, card sliding, bolt tightening) with synchronized RGB, proprioception, and tactile arrays. (2) Compare against ForceVLA-style wrist-force baselines, vision-only VLA, and tactile-only policies. (3) Evaluate generalization to unseen object geometries and textures. (4) Ablate spatial vs. aggregate tactile representations and fusion architectures.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Pretraining with Diffusion-Augmented Sensor Synthesis
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of force-torque sensing for contact-rich manipulation, but 6-axis F/T sensors are expensive, fragile, and provide only global wrist-level contact information. High-resolution tactile sensors (e.g., GelSight, DIGIT) offer spatially-resolved contact geometry but suffer from extreme sim-to-real gaps and scarce real-world demonstrations. We propose TactileVLA, which replaces wrist F/T signals with fingertip tactile images as the contact modality within a VLA framework, enabling richer local contact feedback at lower cost. Method: We train a conditional diffusion model to synthesize photorealistic tactile sensor images from simulated contact geometry, bridging the sim-to-real gap. These synthetic tactile images augment real demonstrations during VLA fine-tuning. A lightweight tactile encoder produces contact embeddings fused into the VLA action decoder via cross-attention, conditioned on language instructions. We also introduce a self-supervised tactile pretraining objective—predicting contact location and normal force from tactile images—to build transferable representations. Experiments: We evaluate on five contact-rich tasks (peg insertion, cable routing, lid screwing, assembly, surface tracing) using a robot hand with DIGIT sensors. Ablations compare F/T-based (ForceVLA-style) vs. tactile-based inputs, synthetic augmentation ratios, and zero-shot generalization to unseen object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates the value of wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensing for contact-rich manipulation, but wrist force sensors provide only aggregate contact information and cannot localize where contact occurs across a robotic hand's surface. Dexterous tasks like in-hand object reorientation, deformable object squeezing, or fragile object grasping require spatially-resolved tactile feedback across dozens of finger and palm contact points simultaneously. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, extending the MoE fusion paradigm to high-density tactile skin arrays (e.g., 64+ taxels per finger). Rather than a single force modality expert, we propose a Spatial Tactile Tokenizer (STT) that encodes tactile maps as patch-based spatial tokens analogous to image patches in ViT, enabling transformer attention to jointly reason over visual, linguistic, and distributed tactile signals. A hierarchical MoE routes computation based on detected contact regions (fingertip, palm, lateral), dynamically weighting experts specialized for precision pinch, power grasp, or sliding contact regimes. We further introduce a tactile-conditioned diffusion action head that synthesizes smooth finger joint trajectories respecting real-time contact feedback. Experiments: We evaluate on five dexterous tasks (in-hand rotation, card sliding, bolt threading, fruit sorting by ripeness, cable routing) using a multi-fingered hand with tactile skin, comparing against ForceVLA, pure vision-based VLA, and ablations removing spatial tokenization or hierarchical routing, measuring success rate, contact force safety violations, and generalization to novel object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensors, but many manipulation tasks (e.g., in-hand re-grasping, garment folding, constrained assembly) require spatially distributed contact information across finger surfaces and palm areas. Wrist F/T sensors conflate distributed contact into a single resultant, losing critical spatial contact geometry needed for dexterous control. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-resolution tactile skin arrays (e.g., GelSight-style or barometric fingertip sensors providing ~100 taxel spatial maps per finger) as a new modality within a VLA framework. Rather than MoE routing on a single force vector, we propose a Tactile Spatial Encoder (TSE) using convolutional processing over tactile maps to extract local contact geometry tokens, which are fused with vision-language embeddings via cross-attention at multiple action-decoding timesteps. A contact-state tokenizer discretizes tactile patterns (slip, shear, normal pressure distribution) into semantic tokens compatible with the VLA's token vocabulary, enabling language-conditioned tactile reasoning. Experiments: We collect TactileVLA-Data across five dexterous tasks (in-hand rotation, card insertion, fabric smoothing, bolt tightening, grape picking without crushing). We compare against ForceVLA, pi_0 baseline, and tactile-only controllers, measuring task success, contact force profiles, and generalization to novel object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Skin-Distributed Tactile Sensing with Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Action Decoding
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, which captures global contact wrench but loses spatial contact distribution information critical for dexterous tasks like in-hand reorientation, compliant grasping of deformable objects, or multi-finger coordinated manipulation. Distributed tactile skin sensors (e.g., fingertip taxels) provide rich spatiotemporal contact maps but introduce high-dimensional, temporally noisy signals that are challenging to fuse with VLA architectures. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-resolution distributed tactile arrays (e.g., 16x16 taxels per fingertip) into a VLA framework using a spatiotemporal tactile encoder based on sparse attention over active contact patches. We extend the MoE fusion concept with a geometry-aware routing mechanism that conditions expert selection on contact topology (point, edge, surface contact regimes) estimated from tactile maps, enabling regime-specific action decoding policies. A contact-regime contrastive pretraining stage aligns tactile embeddings with visual and language representations. Experiments: We evaluate on five dexterous tasks—in-hand rotation, deformable object squeezing, peg-in-hole with angular uncertainty, cable routing, and fragile object grasping—comparing against force-only baselines (ForceVLA), vision-only VLA, and ablations of the geometry-aware routing. Primary metrics include task success rate, contact force profiles, and generalization to novel object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Scalable Pretraining of Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description:
Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, but many manipulation tasks (cloth folding, deformable object handling, multi-contact grasping) require spatially distributed contact information across the robot's entire surface, which a single F/T sensor cannot capture. Existing VLA models lack architectures and pretraining strategies for high-dimensional tactile skin arrays.

Proposed Method: We propose TactileVLA, which incorporates distributed tactile skin sensors (e.g., 64-256 taxel arrays across fingertips, palm, and forearm) into a VLA backbone. Rather than MoE routing over a single force signal, we introduce a Tactile Spatial Tokenizer (TST) that converts 2D tactile pressure maps into patch-based tokens analogous to ViT image patches, enabling transformer cross-attention between tactile, visual, and language streams. We further propose a tactile-masked autoencoding pretraining objective that learns rich tactile representations from unlabeled robot-environment interactions before task-specific finetuning.

Experiments: (1) Collect a TactileVLA-Data dataset of 10 contact-rich tasks with synchronized vision, language, proprioception, and full-hand tactile arrays. (2) Compare TST against F/T baselines and ablate pretraining objectives. (3) Evaluate on occluded grasping, in-hand manipulation, and deformable object tasks. (4) Test generalization to unseen object geometries. Primary metric: task success rate; secondary: contact stability and slip recovery rate.

title: TactileVLA: Unified Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Body Contact Reasoning
description: Problem: ForceVLA equips robots with wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, but this provides only aggregate contact information at a single point. Many dexterous tasks (cloth folding, deformable object manipulation, multi-contact assembly) require spatially-distributed contact awareness across finger surfaces and palm areas that point force sensing cannot capture. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which integrates high-resolution tactile skin arrays (e.g., 16x16 taxel patches per finger segment) as a new modality into a VLA backbone. Rather than MoE fusion of a single force vector, we propose a Tactile Spatial Transformer (TST) module that encodes tactile pressure maps as spatial tokens using a lightweight ViT encoder, preserving contact geometry. These tactile tokens are fused with visual-language tokens via cross-attention during action decoding. We also introduce contact-conditioned action chunking, where predicted action horizons are dynamically shortened when tactile signals indicate unexpected contact states. Experiments: We collect a TactileVLA-Data benchmark with 6 tasks emphasizing spatial contact reasoning: cable routing, garment handling, compliant peg insertion, fragile object grasping, bolt tightening, and multi-finger in-hand rotation. We compare against ForceVLA-style scalar force fusion, proprioception-only baselines, and ablations of tactile resolution (4x4 vs 16x16). Primary metrics include task success rate, contact-induced object damage rate, and generalization to unseen object geometries.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Representation Learning for VLA Models
description:
Problem: ForceVLA demonstrates that force/torque sensing dramatically improves contact-rich manipulation, but 6-axis F/T sensors are expensive, fragile, and provide only wrist-level global contact information. High-resolution tactile skin sensors (e.g., GelSight, DIGIT) offer spatially-resolved fingertip contact geometry but remain underexplored as VLA modalities. Moreover, collecting real tactile demonstrations at scale is costly due to sensor fragility and calibration drift.

Proposed Method: We propose TactileVLA, which integrates spatially-resolved tactile observations into a VLA framework via a sim-to-real tactile encoder pretrained through physics-based simulation. We build a differentiable tactile simulation layer (leveraging FEM-based contact models) to generate synthetic tactile images during visuomotor pretraining, then fine-tune with real tactile data using a domain-adversarial adaptation module. A lightweight cross-attention fusion block integrates per-finger tactile embeddings with visual-language tokens during action decoding, replacing the MoE routing with a spatial attention mechanism that localizes contact regions.

Experiments: (1) Compare against ForceVLA and vision-only pi_0 baselines on peg insertion, bolt tightening, and deformable object packing; (2) Ablate sim-to-real pretraining contribution under limited real tactile data (10/50/200 demos); (3) Test generalization to novel object geometries unseen during training; (4) Evaluate robustness to sensor occlusion and partial tactile coverage.

title: TactileVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Distributed Tactile Skin for Whole-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis force-torque sensing, which captures aggregate contact wrench but loses spatial contact distribution across finger surfaces. Whole-hand dexterous tasks (in-hand reorientation, compliant grasping of deformable objects, handover) require knowing *where* on the hand contact occurs, not just total force. Existing VLA models lack mechanisms to process high-dimensional spatiotemporal tactile arrays from multi-finger skins. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which incorporates distributed tactile sensor arrays (e.g., 5×5 taxel patches per fingertip/phalanx, ~300 channels total) as a new modality. We design a Tactile Tokenizer that applies spatiotemporal convolutions over tactile frames to produce compact contact-map tokens, then fuses these with vision-language tokens via a cross-attention adapter inserted into a pretrained VLA backbone (π0). A contact-conditioned action head predicts both motion and desired contact distributions, enabling closed-loop tactile servo control. Dataset: We collect TactileVLA-Data: 10 dexterous tasks using an Allegro hand with BioTac SP sensors, ~5K demonstrations with synchronized RGB, proprioception, and tactile streams. Experiments: Compare against ForceVLA-style wrist-only force integration and vision-only VLA baselines on in-hand rotation, fragile-object grasping, and tool handover, measuring success rate, slip events, and object damage.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models via Spatial-Temporal Graph Experts
description: Problem: While ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensing, real dexterous manipulation requires distributed tactile feedback across the entire hand surface (fingertips, palm, proximal phalanges). Single-point force signals cannot capture local contact geometry, slip detection, or multi-finger coordination needed for tasks like in-hand reorientation or delicate grasping of deformable objects. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which incorporates a high-density tactile skin array (e.g., 256-taxel glove or fingertip sensors) into a VLA framework. Rather than a generic MoE fusion, we model the tactile array as a spatial-temporal graph where nodes represent individual taxels and edges encode physical proximity. A Graph Attention Network (GAT) encoder produces compact contact-geometry embeddings that are fused with VLA visual-language tokens via a cross-modal attention bottleneck. The GAT experts are dynamically activated based on contact region (fingertip vs. palm), enabling efficient routing without full-graph computation. We construct a dataset of 8 in-hand manipulation tasks with synchronized vision, language, proprioception, and tactile streams. Experiments: (1) Ablate taxel density vs. task success; (2) compare against ForceVLA-style single-point force baselines; (3) evaluate zero-shot transfer to novel object shapes; (4) test slip-prevention in pick-and-place of slippery objects. Target: 25%+ improvement over wrist F/T baselines on in-hand reorientation tasks.

title: TactileVLA: Generalizing Contact-Rich Manipulation via Sim-to-Real Tactile Representation Learning for VLA Models
description: Problem: ForceVLA requires expensive 6-axis force-torque sensors mounted at the wrist, limiting scalability and dexterity for tasks requiring fingertip-level contact resolution (e.g., in-hand object reorientation, deformable object manipulation). High-resolution tactile skin sensors (e.g., GelSight, DIGIT) capture spatially distributed contact geometry but are rarely integrated into VLA frameworks due to sim-to-real gaps and lack of paired language-vision-tactile datasets. Proposed Method: We introduce TactileVLA, which encodes tactile image streams from fingertip sensors via a lightweight convolutional tactile encoder pretrained with a sim-to-real contrastive objective—aligning simulated contact maps (generated via differentiable contact simulation) with real tactile images. The encoded tactile tokens are injected into a frozen VLA backbone (pi_0) through cross-attention adapters, avoiding full fine-tuning costs. A curriculum-based training scheme gradually increases reliance on tactile signals as visual occlusion increases. Planned Experiments: (1) Compare against ForceVLA and vision-only baselines on five contact-rich tasks: bolt tightening, card insertion, grape peeling, cup stacking, and lid screwing. (2) Ablate sim-to-real pretraining vs. real-data-only encoding. (3) Evaluate zero-shot transfer to novel object geometries. (4) Measure performance degradation under camera occlusion at varying degrees, demonstrating tactile compensation.

title: TactileVLA: Unifying Distributed Tactile Skin Sensing with Vision-Language-Action Models for Whole-Body Contact Manipulation
description: Problem: ForceVLA integrates wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensors into VLA models, but wrist forces provide only aggregate contact information. Dexterous manipulation tasks like in-hand reorientation, cloth folding, or assembly require spatially-resolved contact feedback across fingertips and palm surfaces—information that distributed tactile skin sensors provide but no VLA framework currently exploits. Method: We propose TactileVLA, which incorporates high-resolution tactile arrays (e.g., 16x16 per fingertip, 3 fingers + palm) into VLA action decoding. We introduce a Spatial Tactile Tokenizer that compresses tactile pressure maps into learned patch tokens via a CNN encoder, producing spatially-aware tactile embeddings. These tokens are fused with vision-language embeddings using a cross-attention module conditioned on contact region labels (fingertip, palm, proximal), enabling contact-locality-aware action generation. We also investigate whether pretrained vision foundation models can be fine-tuned as tactile encoders via modality-transfer pretraining on paired vision-tactile datasets. Experiments: (1) In-hand object reorientation with varying object geometries; (2) Deformable object manipulation (cloth folding, cable routing); (3) Occlusion-dominant insertion tasks; compared against ForceVLA and proprioception-only baselines. We ablate spatial tokenization granularity and cross-attention locality conditioning to quantify the value of spatial tactile resolution over aggregate force signals.
